sections.title: Layout garden
sections.body: In layout garden you will find a collection of various layouts I found on the internet and tried copying!

sections.heading: Remarks
paragraphs: Let’s see, this one began as a humble attempt to practice my flexbox and grid knowledge by copying various interesting layouts I was to find on my own. This was the first time I was introduced to the php language, particularly through its include method. The approach for this was to have multiple layout 'compartments' one on top of each other that would showcase a uniform design system (the uniformity part of the exercise escaped my attention, a dear mistake as I had to go back and redesign each module multiple times). Another thing I recall (it’s been some time) that caused me some grief was finding a way to target each module’s specific css without having cascading issues. This was addressed through unique elements (or classes) wrapping each module and later used as a selector.

Higher level design concerns ranged from having a tidy css system that one could easily navigate (I’m still working on that), custom variables for colors and margins/paddings as well as some font classes that would add to the concept of a design system. It wasn’t until many months after the first iteration of the garden that I was in a position to go back and judge with a better eye the design concerns relating to each module in particular. Thanks to another DFTW module, the theming layout challenge, I was now able to better appreciate the importance of paddings/margins and the concept of hierarchy, thus another round of stylistic changes took place.

Of course the whole idea behind learning new tricks is applying them wherever you can, enter reusable components. I took the simplistic approach of using php arrays that I would later extract (yes, the php method) to hydrate some skeleton components based on the context of each module instead of using json files . A bit messier but one step less in the process of hydration. At the moment most layouts use components that are reused time and again, or at the very least -in some cases- used for specific layouts and then rendered through a loop!
